description: Saving Tidal Marshes in the San Francisco Bay is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Point Blue Conservation Science; Sonoma Land Trust; California Landscape Conservation and Adaptation Partnership (CAL CAP). As sea level rises, wetlands and marshes must move inland, or drown. The Sonoma Land Trust is using strategies to restore and enhance marshlands and the ecosystems they support. Coverage: the United States (2015). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
